prompts: Use case: scientific-educational. Landscape Study Buddy infographic, Analysis Reporting Lesson 1.4. Title exactly 'Linked, embedded or picture?'. Warm white background, dark navy, muted teal and amber, clean adult study design, generous spacing, highly readable English. Three equal panels with simple file/object icons, never fake Office UI. Panel 1 title 'Linked chart'; show a source workbook connected by an arrow to a chart object in a Word document. Exact description 'Connected to the source workbook'. Exact conditional note 'Source changes can appear after a successful refresh'. Panel 2 title 'Embedded chart'; show a copy of chart and data inside the Word document, no link arrow to the external workbook. Exact description 'A separate editable copy inside Word'. Exact note 'External workbook edits do not update this copy'. Panel 3 title 'Picture'; show an image frame in Word. Exact description 'A static visual snapshot'. Exact note 'No editable chart data or source connection'. Footer exactly 'Test the actual pasted object. Paste options and support vary by Office edition.' Make clear that a linked object may need refresh and a valid source path, not guaranteed immediate automatic changes. No charts with numerical results, invented data, logos, citations or checkmarks suggesting completed work.

Use case: scientific-educational. Landscape Study Buddy infographic for Analysis Reporting Task 1.4. Title exactly 'Four questions, one clear workflow'. Warm white, dark navy, muted teal, restrained amber, adult learning layout, highly readable English. Four numbered panels, each with an icon and short accurate instructions. Panel 'Q1 Insert and test a link' with Excel file arrow to Word chart; text 'Place the chart at the end. Edit the external workbook and check refresh.' Panel 'Q2 Embed and test a copy' with chart inside Word; text 'Use a separate baseline copy. External edits should not change embedded data.' Panel 'Q3 Table and equations' with a table icon and equation editor icon; text 'Enter the supplied rows. Reproduce the equation image and flag unclear grouping.' Panel 'Q4 Captions and three lists' with three distinct list icons labelled 'Figures', 'Tables', 'Equations'; text 'Add captions, then generate and update each list separately.' Include a clearly labelled box 'Required Excel edits' with exactly 'Male users, March: 45,892' and 'Female users, December: 91,364'. These are target edits, not observed chart results. Footer exactly 'Suggested workflow. Verify the saved Office files; record observations, not assumptions.' No fake screenshots, other numerical data, invented equations, automatically checked completion marks or official marking-scheme claims. The Q1 link is the lesson-based workflow interpretation, not a quotation of the official task.
